settings.engine_desc_pw_play: pw-play ● Standard (PipeWire native, no silence trim)
settings.engine_dlg_header:
Linux TTS Audio Engines — Comparison & Recommendations

Currently Detected on Your System:
settings.engine_dlg_body:
★ Tier 1 — Recommended: mpv & ffplay
• Why recommended: Both support real-time hardware-accelerated audio filtering (silenceremove). Microsoft Edge TTS audio files include ~200–400ms of leading and trailing silence. mpv and ffplay strip this silence on the fly, delivering instant, gapless voice announcements with zero delay when multiple users join/leave rapidly, and very low CPU overhead.

● Tier 2 — Standard Native Fallback: pw-play (PipeWire)
• Why worse than mpv/ffplay: Pre-installed out-of-the-box on modern and immutable Linux distributions (such as Bazzite, SteamOS, Fedora Silverblue/Kinoite), allowing TTS to work immediately without extra packages. However, pw-play does not support real-time silence trimming, so announcements have a slight natural pause before and after each phrase.

○ Tier 3 — Secondary Fallbacks: paplay, gst-play-1.0, cvlc
• paplay (PulseAudio): No silence trimming and routes audio through the PulseAudio compatibility layer (pipewire-pulse) instead of native PipeWire.
• gst-play-1.0 (GStreamer) & cvlc (VLC): No silence trimming and noticeably higher process startup latency when initializing the GStreamer/VLC pipeline for every short TTS clip.

Tip for Bazzite / Immutable Linux users: If only pw-play/paplay are detected and you want gapless mpv playback without modifying your read-only root system, you can install mpv in user-space via Homebrew: brew install mpv (then reopen Settings).
